fieldMarks: Stiff spiky tail often cocked upward
Male: dark cap and white cheeks; ruddy body and bright blue bill in breeding season
Female: pale cheeks crossed by a smeary dark line
behavior: Patters across the water to take off and seems reluctant to fly; almost helpless on land
Dives and strains food from bottom mud; insects and larvae are main summer foods
Usually silent; courting males make ticking and clapping sounds
Migrates mostly at night in small flocks
habitat: Breeds on fresh or alkaline lakes and ponds with marshy borders and open water; winters on sheltered shallow coastal bays and ice-free inland lakes.
range: Breeds mainly on the northern prairies, from central British Columbia, southwestern Mackenzie and the Prairie Provinces east across southern Canada to Nova Scotia and south to California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas; northern breeders winter south to Central America.
